Hi Samantha,

Thanks for the flag and for pulling the traces. We're attaching the tabletop log and a snapshot of the DR runbook we used during the exercise. Short answers below and then a slightly longer narrative attached (rpo-variance-narrative.docx).

Quick summary:
- Baseline RPO we target in production: 5 minutes for user session state (tokenized cache), 15 minutes for persistent batch restore targets.
- Observed variances: on March 6 we had two short periods where asynchronous replication lag peaked due to a scheduled caching-layer compaction that coincided with a database maintenance window. The compaction increased write amplification and momentarily delayed background replication checkpoints. Net impact: one ~24-minute window (peak lag ~22 mins) and a second ~12-minute window.
- Root cause: timing overlap between a non-blocking compaction job and a long-running maintenance operation on an auxiliary replica. Both are background ops that normally do not affect foreground replication; the overlap increased IO pressure.
- Remediation / controls: immediate change — we added a jittered compaction schedule and a precedence rule in the maintenance orchestrator so compactions will not start if a replica maintenance job is running. Operational control — added an early-warning metric (replication-lag > 8m) that triggers a prioritized resync job and a runbook play which we include in the attached snapshot.

Attachments included: runbook_snapshot_20270315.pdf (ops runbook excerpt), tabletop-log-march2027.txt (raw audit of the March 6 exercise), rpo-variance-narrative.docx (two-paragraph narrative + control mapping).

We've also mapped the remediation to the SIG questions: C-BC-1 (BC planning — runbook & exercises), C-BC-2 (replication/restore targets — RTO/RPO measurements), and C-BC-4 (continuous improvement / incident follow-up). The attached narrative includes short cross-references.

Priya — thanks for the heads-up. I reviewed the March 6 exercise artifacts and confirmed the timeline. Below is the 2-paragraph narrative and the control mapping bullets you can paste into the evidence bundle. I also screened the tabletop log & runbook excerpt; those are final for distribution.

Narrative (paste-ready):
During a scheduled tabletop on March 6, 2027 the operations team observed two short periods of elevated replication lag that produced transient RPO variance relative to our stated targets. Investigation found the variance occurred when a background cache compaction job coincided with a non-interruptible maintenance task on an auxiliary replica, increasing IO pressure and delaying some background replication checkpoints. No customer-facing requests were lost; client-facing services remained available due to request-side caching and active read replicas.

Remediation and controls: we implemented a precedence rule in the maintenance orchestrator to prevent compaction jobs from starting while replica maintenance is in progress, added a jitter to compaction schedules to reduce collision probability, and introduced a replication-lag early-warning alert (threshold 8 minutes) that auto-triggers a prioritized resync runbook. These steps were validated in a follow-up tabletop on March 14 and are reflected in the attached runbook snapshot.

Control mapping (SIG):
- C-BC-1: Business continuity planning & runbooks — runbook_snapshot_20270315.pdf demonstrates playbook and roles.
- C-BC-2: RTO/RPO definitions and measurement — tabletop-log-march2027.txt contains measurement artifacts and timestamped traces.
- C-BC-4: Post-exercise improvements — rpo-variance-narrative.docx documents root cause and remediation steps implemented.

Let me know if you want this shortened further. I can also prepare a one-line executive summary for the board packet.
